title: A zygote-based assay to evaluate intranuclear shuttling in S. cerevisiae
protocol: Grow two strains of cells, one MAT a and the other MAT α.
Combine 100 μL aliquots of each parental cell strain.
Vortex the combined cell mixture.
Sediment the cell mixtures and resuspend in synthetic medium with 2% glucose at OD600 ≈ 1.
Apply 25 μL samples of mating mixtures to the surface of Petri dishes containing solid 2% agar in synthetic medium.
Cover the Petri dishes after liquid absorption, which should occur within 15 minutes.
Recover the cell mixture by washing with synthetic medium and gentle pipetting up and down 4–5 times after 2 hours at room temperature.
Sediment the cells.
Without removing the supernatant, recover 0.5–1.0 μL samples of the cell pellet.
Apply the sample volume to the surface of freshly-opened Agarose pads.
Cover with a coverslip and observe.
For imaging lasting more than 15 min, trim the pads to the dimensions of the coverslip after adding the cells.
Seal the trimmed pads with vaseline to minimize drying.
Pregrow one or both parental cells that express a tagged protein of interest from a repressible promoter using a medium that allows expression (e.g., with galactose or lacking methionine).
Adjust the composition of the plate used for the cross to repress transcription when preparing the mating mixture, e.g., by adding glucose or methionine.
Pipette the mating mixture off the plate with complete medium.
Add 1/10 volume of formaldehyde from a 37% stock in water, shaking for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash once with growth medium to quench free aldehydes.
Store samples in water at this point for 1–2 days at 4°C before examination.
Transform cells with a centromeric plasmid encoding GFP-HDEL or an integrating plasmid encoding mRFP-HDEL.
Include HDEL marker in both [wt x wt] and [kar1 x wt] crosses.
